title: Tenant Network Field Guide — customer templates & TF notes (draft)
body:
Purpose
-----
This is a lightweight field guide for onboarding customer tenant networks to Redwood Private (VPC / on-prem). It collects reference blueprints, Terraform module notes, and a staged upgrade/migration checklist. Intention: reduce repeated design discussions for common customer patterns, accelerate initial handoffs, and enumerate the upgrade pitfalls we keep hitting.

Scope and audience
------------------
Audience: solutions engineers, infra SREs, platform eng doing customer handoffs.
Scope: network topology recommendations (hybrid and on-prem), terraform module conventions we use internally, staged upgrade steps from older TF modules to the new module set (v2+), and verification recipes. Not a security policy — assume customers will apply enterprise firewall rules as needed.

Quick decision table (pick one)
-------------------------------
- Simple isolated tenant (small PoC): single-VPC, NAT + private egress, peering to Redwood-hosted proxy (use pattern A).
- Production resilient (recommended): multi-subnet multi-az with a transit virtual appliance / managed transit (pattern B).
- Regulated / air-gapped: on-prem with cross-connect and BGP, private-control-plane (pattern C).

Reference Blueprints (textual)
-------------------------------
Pattern A — Lightweight customer VPC (fast start)
- 2 private subnets (app+inference), 1 public subnet for bastion/proxy.
- NAT gateway or customer-managed egress appliance for model download/updates.
- VPC peering to Redwood egress endpoint (if using cloud-hosted breakout) or IPsec to our customer edge.
- Security: centralized SGs for inference nodes, host-level deny-by-default, allow only control-plane IP ranges from Redwood.
Use-case: short PoC, predictable single-AZ capacity.

Pattern B — Production multi-AZ (recommended default)
- 3 AZs with private subnets per AZ (inference, control-plane, infra), explicit route tables.
- Transit/Hub VPC model: customer transit or Redwood-managed transit (depends on contract). We recommend a managed transit for teams that want centralized routing policies and egress controls.
- Autoscaling pools behind a local LB (internal) + health-check subnets. BGP optional for on-prem hybrid.
Use-case: expected throughput, HA and predictable latency SLAs.

Pattern C — On-prem / Colocated (air-gapped friendly)
- Dedicated rack with edge router, BGP session to Redwood edge, reserved VLANs for inference clusters.
- Private control plane: customer hosts the control plane connector or we deploy a lightweight steward VM in the tenant network.
- Artifact distribution: signed artifact bundles over SFTP or trusted internal registry.
Use-case: regulated customers, latent regions, low external internet egress.

Terraform module notes (practical tips)
--------------------------------------
- Module naming: infra-net-tenant_v2 is the canonical module we want teams to adopt. Old modules infra-tenant-net_v1 remain in use but are deprecated.
- Variables we rely on: "environment", "az_count", "enable_transit", "bgp_asn", "customer_cidr_list" — keep defaults minimal, require explicit CIDR input.
- Outputs: export the subnet IDs, route table IDs, and BGP peer IPs (as lists). Avoid nested maps in outputs — keeps downstream lifecycle simpler.
- Sizing: add variable "reserved_ip_margin" to calculate interface allocations for appliances (default 8).
- Naming scheme: ${var.environment}-${local.tenant_short}-${az}-${resource} — consistent across modules.

Common TF pitfalls seen in the wild
----------------------------------
- Cross-account resource creation: customers often give limited IAM perms; require explicit docs for required roles (list in onboarding checklist).
- Changing subnet CIDRs mid-life: causes resource replacement; recommend adding migration step to create new subnets and shift route tables rather than editing existing CIDR.
- BGP peer flapping during staged upgrades: plan for maintenance windows and hold timers.

Staged upgrade plan (v1 -> infra-net-tenant_v2)
-----------------------------------------------
High level steps (staged, safe):
1) Inventory: run terraform state list + map live resources to v1 module outputs.
2) Freeze deployments: scale down autoscaling groups to 0 (or cordon workloads).
3) Introduce compatibility layer: deploy a small module that exports aliases (subnet ids, rtable ids) expected by v2.
4) Apply v2 in parallel with "import" for resources we are reusing. Use terraform import for critical IDs (subnets, route tables, vpc).
5) Repoint routes and peering resources to v2-managed resources.
6) Gradually scale workloads back and monitor traffic.
7) Destroy compatibility aliases and clean up v1 remnants.

Checklist for imports and state work
-----------------------------------
- Capture current terraform state file and back it up.
- Confirm provider versions (we had drift when provider >= 5.0 behaved differently). Document the provider pinned version.
- Use terraform plan with -refresh=false when importing to avoid accidental replacements.
- Run a dry-run traffic cutover in staging (with mirrored routing).

BGP and hybrid notes
---------------------
- Our preferred approach: static BGP templates per customer with pre-agreed ASNs. Standardize on hold-timers: min-hold 90s during upgrade windows.
- IP addressing: allocate /30s for eBGP ptp links. Reserve two /30s per edge for primary+failover.
- Evict policies: prefer route-filtering on the customer edge; we avoid using default-originate unless requested.

Operational verification recipes
--------------------------------
- Connectivity: ping across vpc endpoints, traceroute to Redwood control plane (note: ICMP may be blocked).
- Application-level: run 1k short inference requests spread across AZs and measure p95 latency and error rate.
- BGP: show ip bgp summary on the edge and validate accepted prefixes count.
- Terraform: run terraform plan -> capture exit code, ensure no deletions in plan unless explicitly scheduled.

Example TF snippets (guidance, not copy-paste)
------------------------------------------------
# module invocation (pseudo)
module "tenant_net" {
  source = "git::ssh://git@github.com/redwood-inference/infra-modules.git//infra-net-tenant_v2?ref=main"
  environment = var.environment
  az_count = 3
  customer_cidr_list = var.customer_cidr_list
  bgp_asn = var.customer_bgp_asn
}

# import example (shell)
# terraform import module.tenant_net.aws_vpc.main vpc-0123456789abcdef

Open questions / decision log (draft)
----------------------------------
- Egress model for customers that want to use their own egress proxy vs. Redwood-managed egress — we need a billing/traffic model. (JIRA-8241)
- How much automation to provide for BGP ASN negotiation — manual today, could be automated via a provisioning API.
- Rollback semantics for major TF refactors — what level of automation do we want to keep for safe rollback?

Customer handoff checklist (quick)
---------------------------------
- Collect: CIDR blocks, acceptable maintenance windows, contact POC for NOC, required compliance certificates.
- IAM: request least-privilege roles for infra team (list attached in confluence doc).
- Bringup: schedule 2h initial setup call, 4h staged migration for production.
- Testing: plan smoke tests and perf ramp (1k->10k qps over 24h).

Known caveats and gotchas (war stories)
--------------------------------------
- Some colo providers rewrite TCP MSS causing gRPC fragmentation; add MTU checks early.
- Customers sometimes block ephemeral outbound for artifact download — provide an offline artifact bundle flow.
- TF provider drift caused IAM policies to be replaced; pin providers and document a clear upgrade window.

Next steps (owner: Marina)
-------------------------
- Convert top 3 blueprint text diagrams into actual Confluence diagrams (to share with SEs).
- Add a small test harness that runs the verification recipes automatically during onboarding (prototype in infra-scripts repo).
- Create a customer-facing one-pager that summarizes the three patterns and the expected timeline.

Notes to self / quick TODOs
--------------------------
- Add RFC for egress billing logic (cost split options).
- Reach out to security for recommended network ACL templates.
- Add example BGP config snippets from a real customer (sanitized) into the examples folder.

References
----------
- Confluence: Private Deployments Home (link above)
- GitHub: infra-modules PR 213 (migration notes)
- Jira: JIRA-8241, JIRA-9012 (BGP automation epic)

Last updated: 2024-03-14 (draft)
